compositions.title: Food and water for the journey
compositions.text: Se mann cwæð: ‘Ic wille faran. Mīn scip is gearu. Cumað and helpað mē.’ Twēgen gefēran cōmon tō helpanne. Se mann cwæð: ‘Nimað ðone męte and berað hine. Giefað ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter.’ Se gefēra cwæð: ‘Ic mæg ðone męte beran. Wē sculon ðæt weorc gefręmman.’ Ðā gefēran bǣron ðone męte and gēafon ðǣm fuglum ðæt wæter. Se mann cwæð: ‘Sittað and etað.’ Ðā gefēran ǣton. Hīe fōron.
compositions.intended_meaning: The man said: ‘I want to travel. My ship is ready. Come and help me.’ Two companions came to help. The man said: ‘Take the food and carry it. Give the birds the water.’ The companion said: ‘I can carry the food. We must perform the work.’ The companions carried the food and gave the birds the water. The man said: ‘Sit and eat.’ The companions ate. They travelled.
compositions.reference_limit: Se gefēra identifies a contextual member of the two companions without naming which. Final hīe does not uniquely encode whether the man accompanies them. The food being eaten is a contextual inference; its object is unexpressed.

teaching_examples.text: Ic cann swimman. Hē mæg ðæt wæter beran.
teaching_examples.meaning: I know how to swim. He can carry the water.

teaching_examples.text: Nim ðone męte. Nimað ðone męte.
teaching_examples.meaning: Take the food, one addressee. Take the food, several addressees.

teaching_examples.text: Gief mē ðæt wæter. Helpað mē.
teaching_examples.meaning: Give me the water, one addressee. Help me, several addressees.
Do not drink the water, one addressee.
Go. Do the work well, one addressee.
The ship will be ready, in an explicitly expected later situation.
I know those things, referring to matters already discussed.
